title: Structured Output Validation & Prompt Versioning
description: Enforce strict JSON schema conformance with C# records, validate structured outputs, and manage prompts as code.

data.text: The Need for Guaranteed Schema Conformance

When connecting LLMs to downstream .NET services, databases, or frontend user interfaces, receiving unstructured freeform text is brittle and dangerous. Historically, engineers relied on prompt tricks ('return only JSON, no markdown') which would frequently fail when models included conversational preambles or truncated brackets. Modern AI systems solve this through native Structured Outputs with guaranteed JSON Schema compliance.

data.title: Strict Mode Under the Hood
data.text: OpenAI and Azure OpenAI Structured Outputs utilize constrained decoding: the model's token sampler is mathematically restricted to only emit tokens that satisfy the grammar of the supplied JSON Schema. In .NET, you can generate this schema automatically from strongly-typed C# records.

data.text: Hardcoding prompt strings directly inside C# service classes or React components is an anti-pattern. Prompts are code: they have lifecycle stages, require peer code reviews, depend on model versions, and must be tested against regressions.

data.title: Prompt Management Best Practices in .NET
items: Prompts in Repository (.prompts / .yaml): Store system prompts and templates in dedicated markdown or YAML files committed to Git version control.
Semantic Versioning for Templates: Tag prompt changes with semantic versions (e.g., prompt-triage:v1.2.0); tie evaluations and telemetry spans to the exact prompt version.
Parameter Placeholder Validation: Use strongly-typed template parsers (such as Liquid, Handlebars, or Scriban) that fail during compilation or startup if required placeholders are missing.
Feature Flags & A/B Testing: Deploy new prompt versions behind feature flags (e.g. Azure App Configuration) to route 10% of production traffic before full cutover.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Structured outputs provide mathematical guarantees that LLM responses match JSON schemas
Use ChatResponseFormat.ForJsonSchema<T>() to derive schemas directly from C# records
Never treat prompts as ephemeral text: manage prompts as code with Git versioning
Include prompt version identifiers in OpenTelemetry spans to correlate quality metrics with prompt revisions
Validate deserialized records to ensure domain rules are satisfied before updating databases
data.takeaway: Reliable AI systems bridge the probabilistic world of LLMs with deterministic software. Combining strict JSON schema enforcement with Git-versioned prompt engineering ensures bulletproof integration.
